record.original_question: If n ∈ Z+ with n ≠ 1, is F_n Hopfian (i.e., F_n is not ℓ-isomorphic to a proper quotient of itself)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (an ℓ-group) is a group $G$ equipped with a lattice order $\le$ such that the group operation is order-preserving on both sides: for all $a,b,c,d \in G$, if $a \le b$ and $c \le d$ then $ac \le bd$. A homomorphism of ℓ-groups (an ℓ-homomorphism) is a group homomorphism that also preserves the lattice operations $\vee$ and $\wedge$; an ℓ-isomorphism is a bijective ℓ-homomorphism. An ℓ-ideal of an ℓ-group $G$ is a normal convex sublattice subgroup, equivalently the kernel of an ℓ-homomorphism, and the quotient $G/N$ by an ℓ-ideal $N$ carries a natural ℓ-group structure.

For a positive integer $n$, let $F_n$ denote the free lattice-ordered group on $n$ generators: the ℓ-group characterized (up to ℓ-isomorphism) by the universal property that any function from a fixed $n$-element set into the underlying set of an ℓ-group $H$ extends uniquely to an ℓ-homomorphism $F_n \to H$.

An ℓ-group $G$ is called Hopfian if every surjective ℓ-homomorphism $G \to G$ is an ℓ-isomorphism, equivalently, $G$ is not ℓ-isomorphic to $G/N$ for any nontrivial ℓ-ideal $N$ of $G$.

Question: For every integer $n \ge 2$, is the free lattice-ordered group $F_n$ Hopfian?
artifact.status_search_result: The Hopfian question for free lattice-ordered groups $F_n$ ($n\ge 2$) is recorded as McCleary's Problem 12.52 and appears in standard problem lists on ordered groups; recent literature on free lattice-ordered groups (e.g., work on the space of left orderings, 2009 onward) discusses structural properties of $F_n$ but does not announce a resolution of its Hopfian property. No published solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Free lattice ordered groups and the topology on the space of left orderings of a group
status_evidence.snippet: Studies structural properties of free lattice-ordered groups via spaces of left orderings, without resolving the Hopfian question.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature on F_n addresses related structural questions but does not settle the Hopfian problem.
